text:
deploy-bot: [INCIDENT] auth-proxy: abnormal auth failure rate > 500/min. Trigger: rule/auth-fail-rate. @sam_oncall paged.
sam_oncall: taking this. initial scope: auth failures + possible session replay. @maria_sec can you check logs for token reuse?
maria_sec: pulling last 20m of proxy logs, grep for repeated session ids / odd user-agents.
maria_sec: log sample: ```2026-03-17T12:45:21Z auth-proxy 401 token=svcacct-abc123 ip=203.0.113.45 ua="curl/7.87.0"
2026-03-17T12:45:22Z auth-proxy 401 token=svcacct-xyz789 ip=198.51.100.22 ua="python-requests/2.31"``` looks like svcacct tokens from dev-only IP ranges. not expected.
lee_ops: note: log-forwarder is active to external SIEM and spikes show big batches. can we pause forwarding to avoid leaking sensitive headers?
sam_oncall: agree. lee_ops please run: `systemctl stop log-forwarder.service && curl -X POST https://internal-api/forwarder/pause -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN"`
lee_ops: done. forwarder paused and confirmed no outgoing batches. :white_check_mark:
maria_sec: building token-use map now. suspect long-lived service tokens abused. recommend rotating affected svcacct tokens immediately.
sam_oncall: nina_support looped for customer impact. nina any active customer errors?
nina_support: yes — two customers reported 401s in dashboards starting ~12:46 UTC. marking P1 customer-impact. preparing interim banner and support playbook.
maria_sec: action plan: 1) revoke/rotate svcacct tokens seen in logs, 2) search S3 access logs for possible exposed dumps, 3) open privacy intake and legal loop. I'll start revokes for svcacct-abc123 and svcacct-xyz789.
sam_oncall: revoke command: `POST /internal/v1/service-tokens/revoke {"id":"svcacct-abc123"}` execute and verify auth-proxy rejects old token.
lee_ops: revoke API called for both ids — responses 200. verified auth-proxy now 401s those old tokens. new tokens deployed to services via secure KMS rollout.
maria_sec: scanning S3: found GET to s3://redwood-backups/staging/logs/2026-03-17-12.log from 198.51.100.22. chunk contains base64-encoded debug dumps with Authorization headers intermittently — likely log leak.
legal: automated notice: @maria_sec please open privacy intake ticket with affected customers and timestamps.
maria_sec: privacy ticket opened PRIV-2026-0317, added initial artifacts and S3 paths.
sam_oncall: mitigation status: forwarder paused, tokens revoked, new tokens issued, traffic back to baseline. monitor window 30m.
deploy-bot: [UPDATE] auth-fail-rate alarm cleared at 1767200100.
nina_support: drafted customer notification and CS-SRE review underway. will coordinate release timing with legal.
maria_sec: next steps: add detector for base64-encoded dumps in log pipeline, require scrubber on forwarder to drop Authorization-like strings, and audit long-lived token policy.
lee_ops: will push hotfix to forwarder ACLs to block paths containing "debug" or "dump" and enable scrubber rule. scheduling immediate deploy to staging then prod.
sam_oncall: handoff: I'll remain on watch for 2h. @maria_sec you own RCA + post-incident. @nina_support you own customer comms. page me on any regression.
maria_sec: acknowledged. assembling timeline and initial RCA notes.
nina_support: acknowledged. compiling affected customer list and canned messaging. :white_check_mark:
sam_oncall: closing active pager but keeping thread live for updates. :thumbsup:
